correctness.rationale: A strictly decreasing time path bounds ancestor influence by a summable factorial tail, justifying coupling with isolated exteriors. If the pair is terminally vacant, neither site ever acted as an occupied neighbor, so each rejection came from its own exterior. Conversely, the first accepted central proposal cannot exist if both isolated exterior blockers are present at the specified times. Each blocker test depends on its own half-line and one independent central mark, giving the asserted conditioning factorization for arbitrary measurable terminal half-line events. The endpoint ODE follows by conditioning on its unique arrival and using one smaller isolated half-line before that time. Integrated occupation gives w_A=q(1−S)+C−1 and w_B=p(1−S)+C−1. In W−5(S−1) the constant and degree-two coefficients cancel and every higher even coefficient is positive; the leading ratio is 1/5. For the single vacancy at balance, set z=exp(−1/2), h=1−z, f(t)=1−exp(−t/2), F=∫f=2z−1, J=∫f²=4z−2−z². The single vacancy in the isolated-half coupling is the union of two blockers. Conditioning on the central proposal gives Pr(E_single)=z², the left A joint marginal ((1+2h)F−J)/2, and both A joint numerator hF−J/2. The independent evaluations give conditional covariance −0.043387045680384678… and balanced double-vacancy probability 0.045395125835235592…. Exact finite replay: enumerate binary colorings and permutations on open paths (N=5 and N=6, gap at zero-based positions 2,3), update full path, weight a coloring with k A by 2^k 3^(N−k), retain both vacancies, form total T and joint counts J_lr with marginals L_l,R_r, and verify T J_lr=L_l R_r for every pair. This gave Pr(E)=6/125 and 1/25 respectively, not a substitute for the infinite-line proof. The frozen prose strictly comparing imbalances failed at p=1/2 and lacked absolute values; the repaired finding states the strict magnitude comparison only at unequal bias and correctly records zero versus zero at balance. The coefficient κ is still strictly less than 1/5 throughout (0,1).

value.rationale: Gives a minimal terminal separator in the sense that a pair always separates, while a single vacancy need not. Exact conditional independence for arbitrary exterior observables is useful beyond gap intensity. The best possible factor sharpens distributional separation into a species-resolved law and yields the nontrivial (3/5,2/5) extreme-bias conditional limit; it is not inferred from a density table. Conclusions require this one-attempt nearest-neighbor setting and the stated terminal conditioning.
